summary:
Project Summary

LunaNav is a lunar south-pole landing-site analysis and mission-planning platform using NASA datasets such as LOLA, LROC and SPICE to evaluate terrain, sunlight and Earth visibility.

What Did We Develop?

We are developing eight key features:

1. Dynamic landing suitability heatmap
2. Schedule-slip tolerance map
3. Landing-ellipse robustness assessment
4. Mission failure replay and recovery engine
5. Automatic best-site and backup-site recommender
6. Explainable requirement and failure diagnosis
7. Terrain hazard and landing safety layer
8. Terrain uncertainty and sensitivity analysis

How Does It Address the Challenge?

LunaNav combines terrain and environmental analysis with user-defined mission requirements. It evaluates how landing delays, positional deviations and changing conditions affect site suitability. It identifies failed requirements, explains the reasons and suggests alternative landing dates or backup sites.

 Why Is It Important?

It supports safer landing-site selection, reduces planning uncertainty, identifies potential hazards, improves mission adaptability and provides transparent, data-driven decisions for future lunar exploration.
details:
LunaNav

A landing site may look suitable today, but will it remain suitable when the mission date changes or an unexpected situation occurs? This is the challenge LunaNav aims to address.

01 | THE MISSION: What does LunaNav do?

LunaNav is a web-based lunar south-pole landing-site analysis and mission-planning platform. It transforms lunar terrain and environmental information into an interactive decision-support experience.

Users can explore potential landing locations, select mission dates, examine sunlight conditions, assess Earth visibility and analyse terrain hazards. A dynamic suitability heatmap presents candidate locations as feasible, partially feasible, infeasible or insufficient-data areas.

But LunaNav goes beyond selecting a landing site. It allows users to test whether their plans can withstand changing conditions.

02 | THE WORKFLOW: How does it work?

LunaNav follows a connected mission-planning workflow:

EXPLORE → ANALYSE → STRESS-TEST → DECIDE → RECOVER

  • Explore: Select lunar locations and mission dates.
  • Analyse: Evaluate sunlight, darkness periods, Earth geometric visibility, terrain slope and obstructions.
  • Stress-test: Examine schedule-slip tolerance, landing-ellipse robustness and terrain uncertainty.
  • Decide: Compare multiple scenarios and identify primary and backup landing sites.
  • Recover: Use the Mission Failure Replay and Recovery Engine to introduce hypothetical delays or deviations, identify violated requirements and evaluate alternative plans.

Every assessment is accompanied by explanations of the conditions, thresholds and reasons behind its result.

03 | THE ADVANTAGE: What benefits does it provide?

LunaNav brings several mission-planning factors together in one platform. It helps identify potential landing risks, compare alternative locations and dates, evaluate landing-footprint safety and understand how changing mission conditions affect feasibility. Its explainable analysis makes complex information easier to interpret and supports more informed planning decisions.

04 | THE IMPACT: Why does it matter?

As humanity prepares for future lunar exploration, especially around the Moon's south pole, choosing a landing location is only one part of mission planning. Understanding how that location performs under changing conditions is equally important.

LunaNav aims to support safer, more adaptable and evidence-based mission planning by helping users recognise potential problems early, examine backup options and understand the limitations of their assessments. It can also make lunar mission-planning concepts more accessible to students, researchers and space enthusiasts.

05 | THE TECHNOLOGY: How was it developed?

LunaNav is a software-based web platform developed using HTML, CSS and JavaScript for the web interface and Python for data processing and scientific calculations. The project uses Git and GitHub for version control and team collaboration.

Its scientific analysis is designed around NASA resources, including Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO), Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA), SPICE and JPL resources for lunar terrain and celestial-position information. No physical hardware is required.

06 | THE INNOVATION: What makes it creative?

The central creative idea behind LunaNav is simple: Do not just ask whether a landing site is suitable. Ask whether the mission can still succeed when the plan changes.

Its distinctive approach combines requirement-driven suitability mapping, schedule-slip tolerance, landing-ellipse robustness, uncertainty analysis and hypothetical mission failure replay. Instead of presenting only a score or map, LunaNav explains why a requirement passes or fails and helps users investigate possible recovery options.

07 | THE CONSIDERATIONS: What factors guided the team?

The team considered:

  • Lunar terrain slope, elevation variations and potential hazards.
  • Sunlight availability and prolonged darkness.
  • Earth's geometric visibility and terrain obstruction.
  • Landing-date flexibility and schedule changes.
  • Landing-footprint dimensions and position uncertainty.
  • Data resolution, scientific assumptions and reliability.
  • Computational feasibility, usability and explainability.
